items.title: Every invariant element of a quotient lifts to a monic invariant polynomial mapping to its nth power
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a surjection of rings varphi : A -> B, a finite group G of order n acting on that map, and an element b of the invariant subring B^G, and asserts the existence of a monic polynomial P in A^G[T] which maps to (T - b)^n in B^G[T] (source lines 32539-32545). The construction is explicit: choose a lift a of b in A and set P = prod_{sigma in G} (T - sigma(a)) (proof lines 32547-32549). What has to be checked is that this P really lies in the invariant subring A^G[T], that it is monic of degree n, and that its image in B^G[T] is (T - b)^n, which uses that b is fixed by G so that every sigma acts on b trivially. Those verifications are not written out by the author.
